title: Dynamic Route Performance Workbench & Comparative Chart Specs
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Goal: Design an interactive workbench UI in the Redwood Console that lets operators compare performance across model variants and routes in real time. The workbench should make it easy to: 1) surface latency/throughput/token metrics side-by-side, 2) visualize cold vs warm KV cache effects, 3) show cost-per-1k-token and percent delta when changing batching/quantization, and 4) configure rollout policies from a performance signal. This ticket captures exploratory prototypes, a chart-specs catalogue, accessibility considerations, and design review notes.

Scope: per-model and per-route panes, a multi-series timeline for p50/p95/p99 and throughput, stacked area token composition (prompt vs generated vs cached), and a comparative small-multiples view for model variants. Includes an interactive comparison mode where the user picks up to three routes/models and the workbench normalizes time windows and traffic weights.

Non-goals: implementation of backend aggregation pipelines (handled by ENG-8342) and dedicated capacity autoscaling controls (handled in a follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: Prototype in Figma with interactive flows for: single-route overview, compare-3-models mode, and rollout-trigger panel
Chart spec doc lists encodings, recommended aggregations, default time windows, and axis behaviors
Accessibility checklist completed (keyboard nav, contrast, aria labels) and contrast tokens documented
Design review with PM and two engineers completed and feedback addressed
Usability test with 5 participants (internal product and infra engineers) run and key findings summarized
engineering_notes: Backend will expose aggregated series: p50/p95/p99 latency, requests/sec, tokens_in/tokens_out, cached_hits ratio, cost_per_1000_tokens
Time alignment: use request ingestion timestamp with optional smoothing window (default 1m).
Charting library: prefer existing internal components; ensure support for streaming updates and pause/play scrubber
Rollout integration requires an events API for canary windows (ENG-8411)
review_feedback: PM (Jordan Blake): prefer cost deltas alongside latency to make trade-offs explicit
Eng (Maya Singh): request that p99 be shown as a shaded band rather than a line to reduce visual clutter
Design (Imani Park): increase emphasis on token-type legend and make cached token rows collapsible
Security: confirm no PII in chart tooltips; use hashed route ids where appropriate
decisions: Use small-multiples grid for side-by-side model variant comparisons instead of overlaying too many series
Default time window will be 1 hour with quick presets (15m, 1h, 6h, 24h, 7d)
Show latency quantiles (p50/p95/p99) as layered area + line combo: area for p50-p95, line for p99
Token breakdown will be stacked area: prompt | generated | cached; cached shown as translucent to indicate lower compute cost
chart_specs: Latency timeline: stacked quantile area (p50-p95) with p99 overlay; y-axis in ms (log scale optional toggle); tooltip shows sample counts and median
Throughput timeline: line chart of requests/sec and dashed line for concurrent inflight requests; secondary y-axis for tokens/sec
Token composition: stacked area (prompt, generated, cached) with percent-mode toggle and absolute-token toggle
Cost delta sparkline: per-minute cost estimate normalized to baseline model; clicking opens cost breakdown drilldown
Coldstart heatmap: matrix of start-time buckets vs coldstart latency; color scale uses perceptually uniform map with accessible range
usability_findings: Participants expected a single control to lock time windows across comparisons; added a "time-lock" toggle
Users asked for annotations from releases and rollouts to be visible on timelines; added an annotation lane
People wanted the ability to pin a model as baseline for percent delta calculations
accessibility_notes: Contrast: ensure chart lines meet WCAG AA for 14pt equivalents; provide high-contrast theme toggle
Keyboard: chart series should be focusable and togglable via keyboard; ensure focus ring and aria-expanded states
Screen reader: expose summarized metric cards above charts; tooltips are optional for SR users
next_steps: Incorporate engineering comments and produce final spec for ENG-8342 integration
Run a focused design review with PM, two backend engineers, and the Console accessibility lead on 2025-01-28
Prepare handoff package: figma frames, tokens, chart-spec CSV, and sample mock API payloads
Schedule a 30-minute demo for stakeholders once the prototype is finalized
